Reconcile managedConfigs entries by creating, replacing, patching, linking,
or removing project-owned files for the detected project types. The command
writes those changes and then runs "datamitsu fix" by default. Use --dry-run to
preview without writing or running fix, or --skip-fix to reconcile files without
the post-reconciliation fix.

This command is intentionally separate from project initialization. After
editing datamitsu.config.*, run "datamitsu init" to provision tools, runtimes,
bundles, and .datamitsu links. Use "datamitsu config reconcile" only when you
explicitly intend to rewrite managed project configuration files.

Usage:
  datamitsu config reconcile [flags]

Flags:
      --dry-run          Show what would be reconciled without writing files or running fix
  -h, --help             help for reconcile
      --no-verify-hash   Skip expectChainHash verification even when a pinned managed config drifted from its upstream chain
      --opt-in-tools     Include an all-disabled .datamitsuignore in reconciliation so tools are opt-in (enable them by removing names from the list)
      --skip-fix         Skip running fix after reconciling managed configuration files
      --tools string     Comma-separated list of tools to scope reconciliation to (only their managed config files are considered)

Global Flags:
      --before-config strings   Configuration file(s) to load before auto-discovery (for wrappers/libraries)
      --binary-command string   Override the binary command (for npm package wrappers, etc). Can also be set via DATAMITSU_BINARY_COMMAND env var
      --config strings          Additional configuration file(s) to load and merge (can be specified multiple times)
      --log-format string       Status output format: console or jsonl (also via DATAMITSU_LOG_FORMAT)
      --no-auto-config          Disable auto-discovery of datamitsu.config.{js,mjs,ts} at git root
      --no-oci                  Disable OCI bundle store seeding (also via DATAMITSU_NO_OCI)
      --no-parse                Skip output parsers; show tools' raw output instead (also via DATAMITSU_NO_PARSE)
  -v, --verbose                 Enable debug-level logging (default level is warn)
